discovery: Prediction and observational identification of kilonovae, establishing neutron-star mergers as a cosmic site of r-process heavy-element nucleosynthesis

nominees.name: Daniel Kasen
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Edo Berger
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University / Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: Where the elements heavier than iron, such as gold and uranium, are made was one of the great open problems of physics for six decades. Metzger first predicted quantitatively that the radioactive decay of freshly synthesised r-process nuclei in neutron-star merger ejecta powers a distinctive transient, the kilonova. Kasen showed through atomic-physics-based radiative transfer that lanthanide opacities make this emission red and infrared, providing the decisive observational signature. Berger's team found the first kilonova candidate after GRB 130603B and led spectroscopic and multiwavelength characterisation of the kilonova following GW170817, demonstrating the production of several Earth masses of r-process material. Together these works turned a speculative nucleosynthesis site into a measured one, joining nuclear physics, gravitational-wave astronomy and the chemical record of the oldest stars into a single, data-driven account of the origin of the heaviest elements.
